newsitem.title: GERMANY: VW to study Van Miert aid proposals.
newsitem.headline: VW to study Van Miert aid proposals.

text.p: Volkswagen AG signalled its readiness on Tuesday to compromise in a subsidy dispute with Brussels by saying it would consider further aid-backed investments at its new plants in eastern Germany.

Responding to proposals by European Union competition commissioner Karel Van Miert that extra investment could justify subsidies already granted, VW said it would review its investments at its Mosel plant in the east German state of Saxony in January.
VW has been in dispute with Van Miert over the awarding of 240 million marks in investment help by the state of Saxony for the construction of two car plants.
The German federal government has frozen some of that aid, and a VW spokesman said the company would not draw on it until an agreement is reached with Brussels on the issue.

The VW spokesman decribed as "interesting" suggestions made publicly by Van Miert that further investments in east Germany could justify state aid. Reducing capacity at other plants was another option, although less favourable, Van Miert had said.
